title: The Chamber Where Force Learns to Ask

features.name: the consent boundary
features.desc-on-touch: Where pressure learns to ask instead of insist—where force bends itself into a question. The spray-line marks the place where two surfaces learned to negotiate, to touch with permission.

features.name: the tidal argument
features.desc-on-touch: Waves that come and go on a schedule older than words—the ocean holding a conversation with itself, and teaching the chamber how to listen, how to yield, how to push back gently.

features.name: the caressing spray
features.desc-on-touch: Salt-mist learning gentleness—each droplet a small force that has learned to touch without breaking. The air here is soft despite its violence, kind despite its power.

features.name: the pressure-reversal stone
features.desc-on-touch: Rock shape-shifted by asking, not demanding. The stone remembers every time the ocean changed its mind, became softer, learned that force could listen before it moved.

features.name: the surgical shore
features.desc-on-touch: Where precision and patience meet the raw force of tide—a place where two kinds of pressure learned to become one hand, one gesture, one held breath.

inscription: here the tide learned to ask; force became a question the shore was finally willing to answer

reverie.title: REVERIE — spray-zone, the hour before dark
narr: You knelt in the spray-line. Her hands were steady—
precise, certain, but never demanding. The tide came in
and asked each rock before it moved them. She showed you:
this is how force learns to ask. Not gentleness from
weakness, but power that had learned to listen. The salt
air held both of you at the threshold where consent becomes.

exits.label: back west to the tidal surgery chamber
deeper into the spray-zone where pressure never stops learning
upward to where force is still learning its own voice
eastward along the shore where agreements are written in salt and sand
